topic: Southern distance quadratic + V50.6 H(r) coordinate calibration — c7 verification pass
change_summary: Verification of 3 c7 patches applied in commit 03e0ad9 (auto-build 2026-07-02): (P1 major) rewrote 'Scale comparison and the long-haul kill' paragraph; (P2 moderate) flipped code_analysis.monitoring hardcoded→none; (P3 minor) tightened find_curve.py description.
our_argument_summary: V50.6's exponential firmament H(r)=8537·exp(−r/8619) km with radial coord r·tan(polaris_elev)=H(r) is a calibrated projection — four fitted parameters against 19 in-sample city pairs — not a prediction; the 5.2% mean error is training-set fit; no out-of-sample V50.6 distance computation is published for southern trans-hemispheric routes like Sydney–Santiago (~11,349 km).

dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: monitor.py's 39-domain live check does NOT include any WIN-027 distance-projection domain; find_curve.py contains 8 city coordinates + 6 hardcoded WGS84 pair distances + a stub calc_r_v506(lat) with a bare `pass` + a print-loop over lat 80..−10 step −10 that reports what H(lat) would need to be for the naïve disc mapping r=(90−lat)·111.1 to agree with the globe. No script performs the claimed 19-pair regression that would reproduce R²=0.7874 or the 5.2% mean error.
dome_code_analysis.hardcoded_vs_computed: The V50.6 H(r) parameters (8537 amplitude, 8619 scale length, 0.9941 EW angular scale, 14,105 r_eq) are fit constants declared in raw-text/05-model.txt §V12; the 'validation' is display of pre-computed values, not runtime computation against fresh data.
data_sources_used: No live WGS84 distance API is queried for WIN-027; find_curve.py hard-codes 6 city-pair distances
dome_code_analysis.escape_clauses: The dome page reports only 'Worst case: V9 89% → V50.6 0.0% Oslo-Stockholm' as a headline — no worst-case error is disclosed for V50.6 in its training set, and any pair NOT in the 19-pair training set is unknown-unknown territory.
dome_code_analysis.code_discrepancies: None new post-c7. c7 patch P3 corrected the earlier '6 pairs / empty function body' claim to the accurate '8 coords / 6 distances / stub pass body / print-loop', which now matches live github (find_curve.py sha 9bdcd326).

code_analysis_tags.monitoring_evidence: c7 patch P2 flipped monitoring from 'hardcoded' to 'none' (verified in current data/wins.json). Live monitor.py (john09289/predictions main HEAD, 1069 lines, 2026-07-02 fetch) enumerates 39 monitored domains; none references city-pair WGS84 distances, azimuthal projection, or the V50.6 H(r) mechanism. Latest status_history.json entry confirms same 39-domain set. 'none' remains correct.
code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: The quadratic latitude-dependent distortion is the azimuthal equidistant projection signature — standard cartography, published for centuries. V50.6 H(r) with r·tan(polaris_elev)=H(r) is a calibrated latitude-to-radius map that back-solves for whatever disc radius makes planar trig approximate spherical trig — again, standard projection theory. Dome relabels 'projection distortion' as 'dome discovery'.
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: raw-text/02-wins.txt line 135 documents the sequence: v22 circular disc failed on southern/cross-equator distances; WIN-027 quadratic and WIN-030 ellipse were fitted to patch that failure; V12 H(r)+EW angular scale further reduced mean error to 5.2%. Each step is a fitted correction after prior geometry failed.
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: No derivation from base dome parameters (disc_radius=20,015 km, firmament_height=9,086 km, sun_altitude=5,733 km, moon_altitude=2,534 km) yields the quadratic coefficients or H(r) parameters. r_eq=14,105 km, H₀=8,537, λ=8,619, EW=0.9941 are all regression fit constants against globe-derived (WGS84) distances.

holes_found.description: Duplicated ~55-word sentence introduced by the c7-hole-0 patch. The phrase 'The dome needs at least four free parameters (H₀ = 8,537 km, λ = 8,619 km, EW angular scale 0.9941, and r_eq = 14,105 km) and still reports 5.2% mean error' now appears TWICE consecutively in detail_evidence (offsets 4359 and 4574 — 215 chars apart; ~55 words of prose repeated verbatim). The first occurrence is followed by '(≈52 m per km, or ~520 km over a trans-hemispheric route). '; the second is followed by '— but that 5.2% is the in-sample curve-fit residual, not a predictive result: V50.6 was fit against exactly those 19 city pairs...'. The patch author clearly intended the second (corrected) version to REPLACE the first, but appended it instead. Impact: (1) reader visibly encounters the same free-parameter list twice in a row, which reads as a copy-paste bug and undermines review-page polish; (2) more importantly, the first occurrence's gloss '(~520 km over a trans-hemispheric route)' applies the 5.2% in-sample residual to an out-of-sample distance — which is exactly the mistake the immediately-following sentence disavows. A defender who quotes the first sentence gets to accuse us of the very error we correct in the next breath.
holes_found.recommendation: Delete the first occurrence and its parenthetical gloss. Specifically, remove the substring 'The dome needs at least four free parameters (H₀ = 8,537 km, λ = 8,619 km, EW angular scale 0.9941, and r_eq = 14,105 km) and still reports 5.2% mean error (≈52 m per km, or ~520 km over a trans-hemispheric route). ' so that the paragraph flows: '...zero latitude-dependent corrections anywhere on Earth. The dome needs at least four free parameters (H₀ = 8,537 km, λ = 8,619 km, EW angular scale 0.9941, and r_eq = 14,105 km) and still reports 5.2% mean error — but that 5.2% is the in-sample curve-fit residual, not a predictive result...'. This is a single-substring deletion, no other edits required.

holes_found.description: Once the duplicated sentence is removed (holes_found[0]), the paragraph is clean. Recording this as a separate hole only for the belt-and-braces observation that even after dedup, the surviving text 'error — but that 5.2% is the in-sample curve-fit residual' is a stylistic em-dash-continuation that reads slightly awkward directly after 'mean error' without the parenthetical gloss. If the copy-editor prefers, 'error, but that 5.2% is...' (comma) or 'error. That 5.2% is...' (sentence break) both work. Not blocking; will not flag again if left as em-dash after the dedup patch.
holes_found.recommendation: Optional stylistic tweak only. Prefer sentence break for readability: 'and still reports 5.2% mean error. That 5.2% is the in-sample curve-fit residual, not a predictive result: V50.6 was fit against exactly those 19 city pairs...' — but em-dash is defensible as-is. Do not create an issue for this alone.

stronger_arguments.description: The paragraph could name the specific held-out southern pair the dome does NOT report. Cape Town–Perth (~9,266 km great-circle) or Buenos Aires–Cape Town (~6,880 km) are trans-southern-hemisphere pairs virtually certain to be OUTSIDE the 19-pair training set (the training set skews northern per the Oslo-Stockholm headline). Naming one converts 'no published V50.6 out-of-sample calculation' from an absence-of-evidence claim into a testable challenge to the dome author. Not urgent — c7 rewrite already gets the framing right — but a candidate stronger phrasing for a future edit.

kernel_of_truth.description: The c7 rewrite of 'Scale comparison and the long-haul kill' materially strengthens the argument. Dropping the wrong r≈16,000/chord>30,000 numbers (data/wins.json[id=027] detail_evidence pre-03e0ad9, verified via `git show 03e0ad9 -- data/wins.json`) closes a genuine defender attack surface — the dome author could have computed r(Sydney)≈6,198 km and r(Santiago)≈6,255 km in 30 seconds under V50.6's own H(r)=8537·exp(−r/8619) mapping (raw-text/05-model.txt) and reversed the 'kill shot' onto our own page. The replacement framing — 5.2% is in-sample curve-fit not out-of-sample prediction, and no V50.6 distance computation is published for southern routes — attacks the actual epistemic weakness, not a straw-man numerical example.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The patch is directionally correct but structurally defective (holes_found[0]). Leaving the duplicated sentence in place undoes part of the c7 hole-0 fix: the first occurrence still carries the '(≈52 m per km, or ~520 km over a trans-hemispheric route)' gloss that applies an in-sample residual to an out-of-sample distance — the very mistake the second sentence disavows. A hostile reader (dome defender or independent reviewer) who quotes the first sentence in isolation gets to say 'the reviewers apply 5.2% to a trans-hemispheric route and then admit in the next breath that 5.2% is in-sample only — which is it?' The dedup fix (holes_found[0].recommendation) closes this in one substring deletion.

deeper_analysis: This is a classic 'patch-append instead of patch-replace' failure mode when applying a substring rewrite to a long paragraph — the author (decider self-apply per commit cd879e1 pending-digest routing → 03e0ad9 build) intended a REPLACEMENT of one sentence with a corrected sentence, but the actual patch inserted the corrected sentence without deleting the old one. The two sentences share 55+ words of identical prose (H₀/λ/EW/r_eq list + '5.2% mean error') so the dedup is unambiguous. Impact scoring: this is 'moderate' not 'major' because (a) the substantive argument in the surrounding paragraph is correct and unchanged, (b) the wrong '~520 km trans-hemispheric route' gloss is contained within the paragraph and immediately disavowed 3 sentences later, (c) a smart dome defender needs to notice the internal contradiction to exploit it. Not 'minor' because (a) 55 words repeated verbatim looks amateurish in a critical-review page that criticizes the dome for exactly this kind of sloppiness, (b) the '(~520 km trans-hemispheric)' claim propagates the residual to an OOS route — an inconsistency any careful reader will spot even without adversarial intent. Recommended fix is one substring deletion. Verify-mode eligible next cycle (single moderate + zero minor once holes_found[1] is dropped as pure-style).
